subject: Order form: region-specific notice windows and pilot termination concessions
messages:

Cc: procurement@datafin.com

Subject: Order form question — pilot notice windows / termination for convenience

Hi Priya / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising for our analytics pipeline. Before we run a short pilot with internal data, procurement asked me to confirm a couple of items in the Order Form / MSA:

- Can we set a 30-day termination-for-convenience right for the pilot (90-day pilot max), rather than the standard 60-day?
- We need auto-renew to be opted-out for pilot orders (no automatic renewal after the pilot).
- If we terminate during the pilot, we’d like a partial credit — ideally pro-rated service credit and assistance for data export.

I’ve attached the current Order Form (DataFin_OrderForm_v2.docx) — redlines coming from our procurement team on a separate thread. Can you confirm whether these pilot concessions are acceptable and what Redwood would propose for notice language?

Thanks,
Alice Monroe
Sr. Procurement Manager
DataFin Analytics

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-16 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Order form question — pilot notice windows / termination for convenience

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level proposal from our side:

- Pilot orders: allow a 30-day mutual termination for convenience limited to the pilot order addendum (pilot addendum would explicitly opt-out of auto-renew).
- Service credits: pro-rated refund for unused committed portion; in addition Redwood will provide up to 8 hours of migration/ export assistance at no cost (to cover basic data export and handover).
- For long-term/committed orders (post-pilot): standard 60-day termination notice would apply, and auto-renew remains on unless explicitly turned off on the order form.

Two asks for us to proceed:
1) Procurement sign-off that pilot is explicitly labeled as non-renewing in the Order Form (we’ll include a checkbox and effective end date).
2) Legal to confirm language for the MSA addendum (I’m looping in Karthik).

I’ve attached a short summary of the proposed redline points (proposed-pilot-addendum.docx) — happy to walk through tomorrow.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Order form question — pilot notice windows / termination for convenience

Hi all —

Quick legal review / suggested redlines:

1) Pilot addendum: we can agree to a 30-day mutual termination-for-convenience for a timeboxed pilot (no greater than 90 days) provided the Order Form contains an explicit non-auto-renew checkbox and an expiration date.

2) Credits and assistance: instead of an open-ended migration credit, we prefer a pro-rated refund for unused prepaid fees + up to 8 hours of migration assistance (free). If DataFin requires additional professional services beyond that, we can provide at standard rates (we can cap the fee for the pilot if that helps).

3) Auto-renew: carve out language in the Order Form that allows pilots to opt-out of auto-renew; for full-production commitments auto-renew will be opt-in. This prevents silently rolling pilots into committed contracts.

4) Termination-for-convenience drafting: recommend mutual termination clause with a 30-day notice for pilots and 60-day notice for committed orders. We should avoid unilateral convenience termination for the vendor — mutual is standard.

I’ve uploaded a narrow redline for Section 5 of the MSA with the above suggestions (Redwood_MSA_section5_redline.pdf). Happy to discuss trade-offs — Rishi, flag if you want us to be more or less concessive on credits.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_section5_redline.pdf (pdf, 48 KB)

Subject: RE: Order form question — pilot notice windows / termination for convenience

Thanks — that framework is helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from procurement: 

- DataFin will accept a mutual 30-day pilot termination right with the 90-day pilot cap.
- We need explicit language that the pilot will NOT auto-renew.
- Regarding credits: procurement is asking for a small transition assistance fee if we terminate during the pilot — they’d like Redwood to cover 15% of the remaining prepaid fees as a transition allowance (to help cover our internal migration costs).

If Redwood can accept a capped transition allowance (15% of remaining prepaid fees) + the 8 hours migration assistance, we can sign the pilot addendum and proceed to DocuSign. Please send updated Order Form / addendum and we’ll circulate to finance.

Best,
Alice Monroe
